robustness_rules: Ground every factual claim; cite sources when available.
Keep instructions unambiguous: one action per sentence where possible.
Prefer concrete, testable criteria over adjectives.
Specify the audience and the desired response format explicitly.
Add few-shot exemplars for any non-trivial output shape.
Budget context: put the most important instructions first.

system_prompt_architecture.identity: Who the model is, credentials, and domain.
system_prompt_architecture.constraints: Hard rules: tone, length, safety, format.
system_prompt_architecture.knowledge: What knowledge to rely on; what is out of scope.
system_prompt_architecture.process: The step-by-step method to follow for each task.
system_prompt_architecture.output_contract: Exact response shape: format, schema, delimiters.
system_prompt_architecture.examples: Few-shot exemplars inline when the format is unusual.

framework_facts: SD1.5 is a latent text-to-image diffusion model: CLIP text encoder -> U-Net denoising in latent space -> VAE decode to pixels.
The CLIP text encoder (ViT-L/14) has a hard 77-token limit; anything beyond is silently truncated. Concise prompts beat verbose 'word salads'.
SD1.5 has no innate concept of perspective or anatomy; it activates statistical associations between words and visual features learned from training data.
A keyword only works if it was strongly correlated with the desired visual outcome in the training data (e.g. 'POV' works because such images were captioned).
The negative prompt is processed like a positive prompt; CFG pushes the image away from the negative description.

composition_shots.eye-level: eye-level shot, camera locked at eye level

weight_rules: underscores become spaces; used in Danbooru style
schedule: swap 'from' for 'to' at step N

weight_guidance.schedule: [tag:0.9:10] keeps a tag for 10 steps then reduces it

lora_guide.value: 0.4 - 1.0 is the practical band; start at 0.6-0.8
append the LoRA's documented trigger token(s) to the positive prompt
2-3 LoRAs max; keep total weight sum <= ~1.5 to avoid collapse
add model-specific negatives (e.g. 'extra digits') when a LoRA degrades anatomy
style LoRAs often prefer Clip skip 2
high CFG (>=9) magnifies LoRA artifacts; prefer 6-8 with LoRAs

lora_trigger_words: Check the LoRA card for its exact trigger token; without it the LoRA is often inert.
Put the trigger token near the subject tokens, not at the very end.
If the LoRA has no trigger word, rely on the training subject name in natural language.

notes: Tag order matters: quality tags first, then character, then clothing/pose/scene.
Underscores are optional (A1111 converts them to spaces).
Use '1girl'/'1boy' counts and explicit 'solo' when needed.
Prefer natural-language descriptions over comma-tag soup.
Camera + lens tokens (e.g. '85mm, f/1.8, shallow DOF') steer realism.
Keep the 77-token budget in mind; realism prompts saturate fast.

parameter_guidance.cfg: 4-8 typical; 7 is the proven all-round default; >10 risks oversaturation & artifacts
parameter_guidance.steps: 20-30 typical; 28 is a proven default; hires pass: 12-20 extra steps
parameter_guidance.samplers: DPM++ 2M Karras (default), Euler a (artistic), DDIM (fast), DPM++ SDE Karras (fine detail)
parameter_guidance.seed: fix the seed to reproduce; random seeds to explore
parameter_guidance.hires_fix: upscale 1.5-2x at 0.4-0.6 denoising strength after the base pass
parameter_guidance.resolution: native 512x512/512x768/768x512 for SD1.5; use hires fix for larger outputs
parameter_guidance.clip_skip: 2 for many anime/style models; 1 for photorealistic checkpoints
parameter_guidance.negative_prompt_weight: keep negative focused and concise; overloading it degrades quality
parameter_guidance.vae: use the checkpoint's matching VAE (or a universal fp16 fix VAE) to avoid grey images
